cited_details.statement: The IEEE Communications Magazine has explicitly identified the integration of digital twins (DTs) and artificial intelligence (AI) in 6G as a priority research area, calling for contributions that advance "a comprehensive understanding of the potential and challenges of the integration of DTs and AI in the context of 6G communication systems" [IEEE Communications Magazine CFP, 2022](https://www.comsoc.org/publications/magazines/ieee-communications-magazine/cfp/digital-twins-meet-artificial-intelligence).

The paradigm of edge intelligence has emerged to address these challenges by pushing AI workloads to the network edge, where "edge AI enables low-latency perception by processing data locally, reducing dependence on cloud infrastructure while improving system efficiency" [Zhou et al., 2019](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333733935_Edge_Intelligence_Paving_the_Last_Mile_of_Artificial_Intelligence_With_Edge_Computing).

A 2022 article in an IEEE venue notes that "the paper also highlights the integration of intelligence and automation into DT technology in 6G communication systems" [Kuruvatti et al., 2022](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/iel7/6287639/9668973/09923927.pdf).

Edge-based AI solutions for healthcare monitoring can deliver "a scalable, responsive, and reliable AI-enabled IoT and edge computing-based healthcare solution with low latency when serving patients" [Rathi et al., 2021](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0045790621004699), thereby keeping personal health information local.

In smart healthcare, for example, wearable sensors and medical devices continuously monitor patient vital signs and feed downstream intelligence layers [Rathi et al., 2021](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0045790621004699).

A widely cited survey on edge intelligence defines the convergence of edge computing and AI as encompassing edge inference, edge training, and edge caching of models [Zhou et al., 2019](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333733935_Edge_Intelligence_Paving_the_Last_Mile_of_Artificial_Intelligence_With_Edge_Computing).

The IEEE Communications Magazine has similarly framed digital-twin and AI integration as a 6G research priority, implicitly requiring a network layer capable of distributing intelligence artifacts efficiently [IEEE Communications Magazine CFP, 2022](https://www.comsoc.org/publications/magazines/ieee-communications-magazine/cfp/digital-twins-meet-artificial-intelligence).

In 6G, digital twins can be used to model and optimize the network itself, creating a feedback loop in which the digital representation informs the operation of the physical network [Kuruvatti et al., 2022](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/iel7/6287639/9668973/09923927.pdf).

systematically examines the convergence of edge computing and AI, emphasizing that "edge AI enables low-latency perception by processing data locally, reducing dependence on cloud infrastructure while improving system efficiency" [Zhou et al., 2019](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333733935_Edge_Intelligence_Paving_the_Last_Mile_of_Artificial_Intelligence_With_Edge_Computing).

A 2019 survey documents "the trends in the advancement of edge IoT-based smart healthcare," including the integration of wearable sensors, edge inference, and cloud analytics [Edge Intelligence and IoT in Healthcare Survey, 2019](https://www.academia.edu/60275486/Edge_Intelligence_and_Internet_of_Things_in_Healthcare_A_Survey).

The article "Empowering 6G Communication Systems with Digital Twin" examines how DT technology can be integrated into 6G, noting that it "highlights the integration of intelligence and automation into DT technology in 6G communication systems" [Kuruvatti et al., 2022](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/iel7/6287639/9668973/09923927.pdf).

The IEEE Communications Magazine has issued an open call for papers on "Digital Twins Meet Artificial Intelligence in 6G," underscoring the convergence of DT and AI as a defining research theme for 6G [IEEE Communications Magazine CFP, 2022](https://www.comsoc.org/publications/magazines/ieee-communications-magazine/cfp/digital-twins-meet-artificial-intelligence).

Although a comprehensive ICN survey was retracted in 2022 [Wiley, 2022](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1155/2022/7818712), the broader ICN literature consistently identifies named-data networking as a promising direction for future Internet architectures capable of supporting intelligence-centric traffic.

proposes "a scalable, responsive, and reliable AI-enabled IoT and edge computing-based healthcare solution with low latency when serving patients" [Rathi et al., 2021](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0045790621004699).

A 2019 survey provides a comprehensive overview of edge intelligence in healthcare, discussing "the trends in the advancement of edge IoT-based smart healthcare" and identifying open challenges related to data heterogeneity, security, and regulatory compliance [Edge Intelligence and IoT in Healthcare Survey, 2019](https://www.academia.edu/60275486/Edge_Intelligence_and_Internet_of_Things_in_Healthcare_A_Survey).

The integration of DTs and AI in industrial 6G systems is expected to enable self-optimizing production lines, as highlighted in the 6G digital-twin literature [Kuruvatti et al., 2022](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/iel7/6287639/9668973/09923927.pdf).

- **Resource Orchestration and Model Placement.** Efficiently placing and migrating AI models across edge, fog, and cloud resources is a complex optimization problem that depends on workload characteristics, network conditions, and energy constraints [Zhou et al., 2019](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333733935_Edge_Intelligence_Paving_the_Last_Mile_of_Artificial_Intelligence_With_Edge_Computing).

- **Network-Native Intelligence.** Embedding AI into the network infrastructure itself—enabling self-optimizing, self-healing 6G networks—remains a long-term research challenge that requires advances in both AI and networking [Kuruvatti et al., 2022](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/iel7/6287639/9668973/09923927.pdf).

evidence.title: Trusted AI in Multi-agent Systems: An Overview of Privacy and Security for Distributed Learning
evidence.abstract: Motivated by the advancing computational capacity of distributed end-user equipments (UEs), as well as the increasing concerns about sharing private data, there has been considerable recent interest in machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) that can be processed on on distributed UEs. Specifically, in this paradigm, parts of an ML process are outsourced to multiple distributed UEs, and then the processed ML information is aggregated on a certain level at a central server, which turns a centralized ML process into a distributed one, and brings about significant benefits. However, this new distributed ML paradigm raises new risks of privacy and security issues. In this paper, we provide a survey of the emerging security and privacy risks of distributed ML from a unique perspective of information exchange levels, which are defined according to the key steps of an ML process, i.e.: i) the level of preprocessed data, ii) the level of learning models, iii) the level of extracted knowledge and, iv) the level of intermediate results. We explore and analyze the potential of threats for each information exchange level based on an overview of the current state-of-the-art attack mechanisms, and then discuss the possible defense methods against such threats. Finally, we complete the survey by providing an outlook on the challenges and possible directions for future research in this critical area.

evidence.title: Privacy-preserving Artificial Intelligence Techniques in Biomedicine
evidence.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been successfully applied in numerous scientific domains. In biomedicine, AI has already shown tremendous potential, e.g. in the interpretation of next-generation sequencing data and in the design of clinical decision support systems. However, training an AI model on sensitive data raises concerns about the privacy of individual participants. For example, summary statistics of a genome-wide association study can be used to determine the presence or absence of an individual in a given dataset. This considerable privacy risk has led to restrictions in accessing genomic and other biomedical data, which is detrimental for collaborative research and impedes scientific progress. Hence, there has been a substantial effort to develop AI methods that can learn from sensitive data while protecting individuals' privacy. This paper provides a structured overview of recent advances in privacy-preserving AI techniques in biomedicine. It places the most important state-of-the-art approaches within a unified taxonomy and discusses their strengths, limitations, and open problems. As the most promising direction, we suggest combining federated machine learning as a more scalable approach with other additional privacy preserving techniques. This would allow to merge the advantages to provide privacy guarantees in a distributed way for biomedical applications. Nonetheless, more research is necessary as hybrid approaches pose new challenges such as additional network or computation overhead.
